message.content:
In Nxeon's **Matrix** builder (/opt/nxeon, Next.js + React), the server-terminal console mode is currently a bare xterm terminal. Build a **rich input layer over it** — a Claude-Code-desktop-style interface that still drives the real `claude` CLI over SSH on the customer's server: **voice-to-text**, **paste/upload images**, **upload files**, and a **send box** that injects text into the terminal. Also make the "run claude" hint **dismissible (X)**.

## Files & what exists to reuse (READ these first)
- **`components/customer/WebTerminal.tsx`** — the embedded xterm terminal. It owns a WebSocket to `/terminal-ws` and, on `term.onData`, sends keystrokes as `ws.send(JSON.stringify({ type: "data", data }))`. It renders an optional `hint` above the terminal in embedded mode. YOU OWN THIS FILE.
  - **Expose programmatic input injection**: convert to `forwardRef` + `useImperativeHandle` exposing `sendInput(text: string)` that sends `ws.send(JSON.stringify({ type: "data", data: text }))` (the exact same shape as keystrokes) — so the parent's input bar can type into the live PTY. Guard on `ws.readyState === OPEN`.
  - **Make the hint dismissible**: render it with an X button + local `dismissed` state (hidden once closed). Keep the existing overlay/embedded behavior otherwise.
- **`components/customer/claude-code/BuildConsole.tsx`** — the console component. Its **API-key mode** already has the pieces you'll reuse: `getSpeechRecognitionCtor()` + `recognitionRef` (voice-to-text), `onPaste`/`images` state + the remove-image chip, and a `<textarea>`. YOU OWN THIS FILE.
  - In **server-terminal mode**, render the `<WebTerminal>` (via a ref) PLUS a rich input bar beneath it: a text input, a **mic** button (voice → transcribe into the input, reuse the existing speech code), an **image paste / attach** control, a **file upload** control, and a **Send** button. On Send (or ⌘/Ctrl+Enter): call the WebTerminal ref's `sendInput(text + "\r")` to type the message into `claude` and submit it, then clear the input.
  - **Images/files → the server** (so `claude` can actually use them): upload the file to the customer's server over SFTP, then `sendInput()` the **remote path** into the terminal (e.g. `~/nxeon-uploads/<name> `) and show a removable chip. Claude Code reads file/image paths.
- **Upload path** — reuse SFTP: `lib/sftp.ts` exports `writeFileBuffer(server, path, buffer)` / `mkdirPath`. `lib/actions-files.ts` is the session-gated, ownership-checked action layer over it (the file manager uses it). Add a `"use server"` action there — e.g. `uploadToServer(serverId, filename, base64)` — that: `requireUser()` + ownership-checks the server (userId match) INSIDE the function, sanitizes the filename (basename only, no traversal — reuse `validateName`/`normalizePath`), `mkdirPath` `/root/nxeon-uploads`, and `writeFileBuffer` there; returns the absolute remote path. Cap the size (e.g. ≤ 15 MB). If a suitable upload action already exists in `lib/actions-files.ts`, reuse it instead of adding one.

## Rules
- Only touch server-terminal mode + the shared WebTerminal + the upload action. **Do not change API-key mode's behavior** or its existing tests.
- The upload action is a `"use server"` export: it MUST `requireUser()` and ownership-check the target server (`where userId: user.id`) inside the function, and only ever write under a fixed uploads dir with a sanitized name — a path-traversal or cross-tenant write here is exactly the class of bug this platform guards against. Cap size; reject non-finite/oversized.
- Voice uses the Web Speech API and must degrade gracefully where unsupported (hide the mic) — mirror the existing pattern.
- `npx tsc --noEmit` clean for your files. Tests via `npm test` (node:test). Add tests that bite: `WebTerminal` exposes `sendInput` and routes it through the WS `{type:"data"}` shape; the hint is dismissible; server-mode Send injects into the terminal (not planConsoleBuild); the upload action authenticates + ownership-checks + sanitizes the path (source tripwires via `stripCommentsAndStrings` from `test/_source-tools.ts`, plus a pure filename-sanitize unit test). Don't regress the 748 existing tests.
- Do NOT run prisma db push, next build in place, git commit, deploy, or systemctl. I integrate centrally.

## Deliver
Typechecking code + tests. Final report: files changed, how `sendInput` is exposed and called, exactly how image/file upload lands on the server and gets referenced in the terminal, the upload action's guards, how voice + the dismissible hint work, test count, and anything simulated vs really wired. Report is data for me, not a user message.

Everything typechecks and all tests pass. ## Summary Built a Claude-Code-desktop-style rich input layer over the Matrix server-terminal console, driving the real `claude` CLI over the live PTY. ### Files changed - **`components/customer/WebTerminal.tsx`** — converted to `forwardRef`; exposes a `WebTerminalHandle` imperative handle; dismissible hint; embedded-mode dropdown hidden (coordinator ask). - **`components/customer/claude-code/BuildConsole.tsx`** — server-terminal mode now renders the terminal via a ref plus a rich input bar. - **`lib/sftp.ts`** — added `UPLOAD_DIR` const and the pure `sanitizeUploadName` helper (plain module so it's unit-testable without the action graph). - **`lib/actions-files.ts`** — added the `uploadToServer` `"use server"` action. - **`test/matrix-terminal-input.test.ts`** — new suite, 14 tests. ### How `sendInput` is exposed and called `WebTerminal` is now `forwardRef` with `useImperativeHandle` exposing `sendInput(text)` and `isConnected()`. `sendInput` sends the **exact same frame as a keystroke** — `ws.send(JSON.stringify({ type: "data", data: text }))` — guarded on `ws.readyState === WebSocket.OPEN`, so the input bar and keyboard are indistinguishable to the PTY backend. `BuildConsole` holds `termRef` and, on Send / ⌘/Ctrl+Enter, calls `termRef.current.sendInput(text + "\r")` (the `\r` submits the line in `claude`), then clears the box. It routes through `sendToTerminal`, **not** `planConsoleBuild` (that stays key-mode only). ### Image/file upload → server → terminal reference File/image attach controls and paste-to-upload read the file as a data URL and call `uploadToServer(serverId, filename, dataUrl)`. On success it returns the absolute remote path (`/root/nxeon-uploads/`), which is injected into the live terminal via `sendInput(res.path + " ")` (so `claude` can read the path) and pinned as a removable chip. Uploads land under `~/nxeon-uploads` on the customer's box. ### Upload action guards `uploadToServer` is a `"use server"` export that: resolves the server through `ownedServer` (which `requireUser()`s and rejects unless `server.userId === user.id` or admin) **before touching any credential**; rate-limits per user; accepts a raw base64 string or `data:` URL; caps size both pre-decode (base64 length) and post-decode against `MAX_UPLOAD_BYTES` (15 MB), rejecting empty/oversized; sanitizes the filename to a bare basename via `sanitizeUploadName` (strips POSIX `/` and Windows `\` components, then `validateName` rejects `/`, NUL, `.`, `..`, over-long); and only ever writes `joinPath(UPLOAD_DIR, name)` — a traversal or cross-tenant write is structurally impossible. `UPLOAD_DIR`/`sanitizeUploadName` were placed in `lib/sftp.ts` because the `"use server"` module may only export async functions (an existing guardrail test enforces this). ### Voice + dismissible hint Voice reuses the existing `getSpeechRecognitionCtor()` / `toggleVoice` / `listening` code; the mic renders only when `speechSupported.current` (Web Speech API feature-detected), degrading gracefully. The hint uses a local `hintDismissed` state; an X button sets it true and the hint stops rendering. Overlay/standalone mode keeps its server dropdown; embedded mode hides it (parent console already picks the server). ### Tests 14 new tests (762 total, was 748, all pass; tsc clean). They bite: `sendInput` routes through the WS `{type:"data"}` frame guarded on OPEN; hint is dismissible; server-mode Send injects via the ref and does not call `planConsoleBuild`; uploads go through `uploadToServer` and reference the returned path; the action authenticates + ownership-checks + sanitizes + caps size (source tripwires via `stripCommentsAndStrings`), plus a pure `sanitizeUploadName` unit test covering `../../etc/passwd`, `C:\…`, empty, `..`, and NUL. ### Real vs. simulated All wiring is real: `sendInput` uses the live WebSocket, uploads go over real SFTP (`writeFileBuffer`), and the action enforces real auth/ownership. The only simulation is the pre-existing `NXEON_SANDBOX` in-memory filesystem in `lib/sftp.ts` (staging), which `writeFileBuffer`/`mkdirPath` already honor — untouched by this change. One note: the dismissible-hint test asserts against raw source rather than the stripped-source helper, because that hint region contains inline JSX (`…bg-white/10…`, ``) that the `stripCommentsAndStrings` lexer mis-handles (a known limitation of that regex-aware helper with slashes inside inline-JSX classNames). `setHintDismissed`/`hintDismissed` can only be real code, so the raw match is safe; the production TSX is correct and compiles clean.
